children: STOCKHOLM--Saab said Thursday that The Netherlands has signed a letter of intent for the acquisition of a GlobalEye surveillance aircraft.
The Swedish defense company said the parties have not yet entered into a contract and Saab has not yet received an order from The Netherlands.

"The system will provide enhanced situational awareness and early warning capabilities across multiple domains, while also strengthening NATO's ability to operate in an increasingly complex security environment," Saab Chief Executive Micael Johansson said.
Saab's GlobalEye is a command and control system that combines radar and sensors built on a Bombardier jet, providing long-range detection and identification of objects in air, at sea and over land.

The Netherlands ministry of defense said in a statement that the Dutch aircraft would be added to a joint pool with three Swedish GlobalEye aircraft, ensuring that Dutch and Swedish crews have access to the available aircraft.
"Both countries are also working together on the further development of the system," the ministry said in a statement.

The platform was recently selected by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization as part of its plans to modernize and strengthen its surveillance and situational-awareness capabilities, with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte announcing the alliance would start formal talks to buy up to 10 GlobalEye systems.
Since the NATO announcement, Saab has also secured an order worth around $1 billion for two of the aircraft from a country in the Middle East region.

title: The Netherlands Announces Intention to Acquire a Saab GlobalEye Surveillance Aircraft
